exposure: Integrated post-partum family planning (PPFP) and maternal and newborn health (MNH) interventions
cohort: Women in 8 unions (population ~25,000 each) in rural Bangladesh, allocated to either an integrated post-partum family planning and maternal and newborn health intervention group or a control group receiving only maternal and newborn health interventions.
finding: Integrating post-partum family planning into a community-based maternal and newborn health program resulted in a 19% lower risk of short birth intervals and a 21% lower risk of preterm birth compared to the control arm.
